subject: Automotive & EVs
title: Cell Form Factors
description: A quick, practical guide to Cell Form Factors.

hook.text: EV battery cells come in three shapes—cylindrical cans, flat pouches, and rectangular prisms.

buildup.text: Cylindrical cells are cheap and proven—Tesla built its empire on thousands of small round cans.

discovery.text: Pouch cells are thin and flexible, letting designers fit batteries into tight or unusual spaces.

twist.text: Prismatic cells are rigid blocks that stack neatly but cost more to manufacture than cylinders.

climax.text: Tesla's new 4680 cylindrical cell is six times larger, aiming to combine cylinder cost with prismatic density.

punchline.text: The shape of the cell shapes the design of the entire car.

quiz.question: Which cell form factor did Tesla originally build its EVs around?
